items.title: Closed Session

expected_flags.summary: Closed-session posted under blanket §§551.071–551.087 range — presiding officer should state specifics on the record before entering.
expected_flags.evidence_quote: K. CLOSED SESSION, PURSUANT TO TEXAS GOVERNMENT CODE, SECTIONS 551.071 THROUGH 551.087

expected_flags.summary: Closed-session posted under the full §551.071–§551.087 range without specifying which subsections actually apply tonight.

§551.074 (personnel) covers specific individuals by name or position only; if discussion tonight veers into general employment policy, working conditions, or salary schedules, it must return to open session.

expected_questions: Will the board president state the SPECIFIC TGC sections (not just the blanket range) before entering closed session?
Is the certified agenda and audio recording being maintained as required by TGC §551.103?
Which specific exceptions are anticipated tonight — personnel (§551.074) related to the teacher contracts? Real property (§551.072)? Litigation (§551.071)?
If the closed session involves personnel evaluations, have the affected employees been notified of their right to request a public hearing under TGC §551.074(b)?

items.title: Bond Series 2026 Parameter Order

expected_flags.summary: This is a debt RESTRUCTURING, not a savings refunding. Samco analysis shows zero debt service savings; total hold-harmless cost is $32.2M; total net debt service is $164.4M.
expected_flags.evidence_quote: WHEREAS, the Board has taken into account the negative aspects of issuing the Bonds and the restructuring and refunding of the Refunded Obligations at a loss

expected_flags.summary: Execution authority delegated to Pricing Officer with dollar ceiling ($5M max gross loss, 6% TIC cap) and one-year expiration, but no explicit report-back to the Board on final terms.
expected_flags._override_applied: 2 of 3 disqualifier elements present → WATCH (not RED_FLAG)

expected_flags.summary: I&S Fund Balance declined 80% in three years ($1.94M → $389K); refunding draws another $2M from it over four years.
$32.2M hold-harmless dependency over 22 years — Hold Harmless is a statutory construct (HB3 2019, HB2 2023), not a constitutional guarantee.
Same annual parameter order authorized last May; recurring annual refunding authorizations suggest structural mismatch between debt service costs and the $0.50 I&S rate.
expected_flags.evidence_quote: This is the same action we took last year in May in the event we may need to refund/restructure our bond payments. Last year's Order expires at the end of April, so we are simply renewing this one-year order in the event we need to refund/restructure.

expected_flags.summary: Parameter Order §3(c) authorizes Capital Appreciation Bonds; total compounded cost is not disclosed.
expected_flags.evidence_quote: The Bonds may be issued in one or more series as Current Interest Bonds or Capital Appreciation Bonds, or a combination thereof, as set forth in the Pricing Certificate.

expected_flags.summary: Agenda title references Series 2016 and Series 2017 but the parameter order's Schedule I and the Samco analysis also include Series 2015.
Combined legislative dependency: $32.2M Hold Harmless on the bond side plus $1.18M/yr restricted HB2 allotments on the budget side — a single legislative session could alter both funding streams.

expected_question_themes: confirmation that debt service savings column is zero
legislative-risk stress test on Hold Harmless (25% / 50% reductions)
minimum safe I&S fund balance and timing
PCAD certified values (April 24) seen before Pricing Officer executes
taxable value growth at 0% or negative scenario
multi-year debt management strategy vs annual parameter orders
Capital Appreciation Bond contemplation
6% TIC cap vs current market
combined General Fund + I&S reserves adequacy
downside of passing the order and not executing
